key_insight: Combine the strengths of continuous diffusion (precise kinematics) and discrete token generators (robust semantic conditioning) via a three-stage pipeline centered on MoTok, a diffusion-based discrete motion tokenizer that decouples semantic and kinematic factors.
problem_solved: Existing motion generation methods excel at either kinematic fidelity (continuous diffusion) or semantic conditioning (discrete tokens) but struggle to satisfy both simultaneously; this work bridges that gap to produce motions that are both semantically aligned and kinematically accurate.
method: Perception: extract condition features (e.g., text, intent, or scene cues) that encode semantic instructions and kinematic hints.
Planning: use MoTok — a diffusion-based discrete motion tokenizer — to generate discrete motion tokens that separate semantic content from low-level motion details.
Control: synthesize final continuous motion via a diffusion-based conditional decoder that reconstructs high-fidelity kinematics from the generated tokens and condition features.
impact: Enables controllable motion generation that is simultaneously semantically faithful and kinematically realistic, improving downstream applications like character animation, virtual avatars, and robotics motion planning.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: three stacked blocks labeled Perception → Planning (MoTok) → Control, showing flow from semantic input to discrete tokens to continuous motion output.
Tokenization schematic: side-by-side animation frames and their corresponding discrete token sequence to illustrate compression and decoupling.
Comparison chart: qualitative/metric trade-offs between Continuous-only, Discrete-only, and the proposed hybrid approach (accuracy vs. semantic alignment).
Sample grid: input semantic prompts (text/labels) next to generated motion clips or pose sequences demonstrating improved alignment and kinematic fidelity.
paper_title: Bridging Semantic and Kinematic Conditions with Diffusion-based Discrete Motion Tokenizer
paper_authors: Chenyang Gu, Mingyuan Zhang, Haozhe Xie, Zhongang Cai, Lei Yang
